A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original HH-RLHF and Reddit TL;DR alignment experiments, GPT-4 evaluations, feedback analyses, and supplementary experiments in Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results, including the main benchmark comparisons and appendix ablations.

M1.justification: Section 3.1 retains the same weak-model SFT/DPO training, preference labeling using implicit rewards, and student SFT/DPO on weak feedback. Equations 4–6 and the labeling procedure are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate HH-RLHF dialogue alignment and Reddit TL;DR summarization. No datasets, tasks, or distinct test scenarios are added or removed, including in the appendices.

E2.justification: The human-feedback comparisons and OPT-125M, OPT-1.3B, Llama-3-8B, and GPT-4 supervisor comparison are unchanged. Table 12 retains the same GPT-Neo-125M and Pythia-160M comparisons, and appendix controls retain their membership.

E3.justification: Data filtering and splits, student model configurations, evaluation metrics, the 100-prompt GPT-4 evaluation, training hyperparameters in Tables 7–8, and decoding settings in Appendix A are unchanged.

E4.justification: Both retain the feedback-match and random-noise controls, data-size and SFT ablations, KL-coefficient sensitivity analysis, alternative reward-model evaluations, generation correlations, and qualitative examples in Sections 3–4 and Appendices B–C.

E5.justification: Appendix C retains seed 22, five additional random splits, and the same mean/variance reporting. Section 4 retains ten consecutive GPT-4 judgments per sampled example. No statistical reporting procedures are added or revised.

E6.justification: Numerical results and qualitative findings match throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Figure 2(a) retains OPT-1.3B rewards of 4.84 versus 4.63 for weak versus human feedback, and Table 5 retains consistency values of 0.84 and 0.66.

T1.justification: Definition 2.1, the RLHF/DPO objectives, implicit reward, and preference-label rule are unchanged. Neither version contains additional original theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same contributions and claims about weak feedback matching or exceeding human feedback and the limited influence of supervisor size. The added conclusion restates these claims without changing their scope.

C2.justification: Interpretations involving imperfect human labels, subtle response-quality differences, and GPT-4 inconsistency are unchanged. Section 5's critique of accuracy-based evaluation and Appendix D's limitations and future directions are also retained.

D1.justification: v2 adds an explicit public-code availability statement and project-repository link in the abstract, absent from v1. Appendix A's implementation, hardware, hyperparameter, preprocessing, and evaluation disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged, including the distinction from Burns et al. in Section 5 and the related-work discussion in Section 6. Reference differences are typographical and due to reflow.

P1.justification: v2 adds a short Section 7 Conclusion and adds Wendi Li to the acknowledgments. Existing sections and Appendices A–D retain essentially identical prose and ordering, with minor front-matter and heading edits.

P2.justification: The ICLR template changes title/abstract placement, margins, headers, typography, and the sizing and spacing of existing displays. All seven figures and twelve tables are retained with unchanged graphical content, captions, axes, legends, and table organization.

improvement.justification: The added project-code link improves reproducibility information, and the new conclusion provides an explicit synthesis of the findings. These are limited documentation and presentation gains; the methods, empirical evidence, interpretations, and stated limitations remain unchanged.
